Mark a START and an END first: turn the dial, then tap the cards.
START and END are at the same spot. Move the dial and mark one again.

Phone is using its %d mm lens
At this zoom the phone picked its %1$d mm lens instead of the %2$d mm one. Phones often do this when focusing very close. Photos are a crop of that lens, and RAW files show its whole frame.
JPEG: ready-to-use photos, small files, fastest bursts.
RAW: untouched sensor data (DNG), like Pro mode\'s RAW. Best for editing and stacking. About 24 MB a photo.
RAW + JPEG: a DNG for stacking, plus a JPEG to check quickly.
Fast: shoots the whole stack as one continuous burst, like a camera\'s focus bracketing.
Precise: stops and checks the lens before every photo. Slower, but use it if Fast gives soft frames.
The merged photo appears here as it builds
Shoot a stack and the phone merges it into one photo that\'s sharp from front to back. It\'s saved in Pictures/MacroStack/Stacked.
%d photo(s) couldn\'t be aligned. Check the result\'s edges.
Merged at a smaller size to fit in memory.
Depth map (like Zerene DMap / Helicon Method B): least noise, and no ghosted outlines if something moved. Best for most stacks.
Pyramid (like Zerene PMax / Helicon Method C): the finest detail where hairs and bristles cross, but a little noisier, and it can ghost if the subject moved.
Merge your last stack (%s) into one sharp photo.
Merge each stack into one sharp photo
Runs in the background right after shooting, in about 0.6–1 s per photo. The result goes to Pictures/MacroStack/Stacked, and your original frames are kept, so you can still stack them on a laptop.
The camera meters the scene, then locks exposure and white balance when the stack starts, so every frame matches.
Shutter speeds slower than 1/30 s also slow Fast mode down.
Maximum uses the full sensor (e.g. 50 or 200 MP) but is many times slower.
Frames the focus motor gets to arrive before each photo. Raise this if some frames are soft.
Raise this if some frames are soft or shaky.
Lets vibrations from pressing the shutter die down.
Volume keys and Bluetooth remotes start a stack
Beep when a stack is done
Turn this off when the phone is on a tripod.

string-array.name: help_steps
string-array.item: Tap the lens your macro attachment is clipped onto, and put the phone on a stand.
Turn the focus dial until the nearest part of the subject is sharp. Peaking marks sharp edges. Then tap START.
Turn it until the farthest part is sharp, then tap END.
Pick how many frames, then press the shutter (or a volume key, or a Bluetooth remote). Don\'t touch the phone until it beeps.

resources.string: Right after shooting, the phone merges the stack into one sharp photo. Watch it build with the thumbnail next to the shutter. Results go to Pictures/MacroStack/Stacked, and the original frames stay in their own folder for laptop stacking.\n\nTap the strip above the dial to jump across the focus range, and double-tap the preview to magnify.
What this phone lets apps do with each lens. Copy it and send it along if something doesn\'t work.
